audit.whatIsWrong: content.whys[1] told the player "my Q blind is only online if he auto-attacks, which he doesn't need to do to hurt me", framing Blinding Dart as close to useless here.
audit.why: That inverts the matchup. Staggering Blow — the root that makes Nautilus's whole combo work — is a basic-attack passive, and the wiki states it "will fail to trigger while he is blinded". Blinding Dart is therefore the single strongest button Teemo has in this lane: hook lands, blind goes out, no root, no follow-up chain.
audit.corrected: Blind him as the anchor connects — Staggering Blow fails while he is blinded, so the pull leads nowhere.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.whys[3] described Nautilus chaining "E slow into a passive re-root" inside a single levels 4-5 combo.
audit.why: Staggering Blow has a 6-second per-target immunity, so it cannot root the same target twice inside one combo. A player told to expect a second root will hold Move Quick for CC that is never coming, and waste the window where he is actually free to walk out.
audit.corrected: There is no second root in that sequence — once Staggering Blow has fired on you, you have 6 seconds before it can apply again.

audit.whatIsWrong: Dredge Line was tracked qualitatively ("His only engage. Dodge it.") with no cooldown attached, and the packet counted one sequencing cue in the whole matchup.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10s and stops on the first enemy or terrain it hits. A missed hook at rank 1 hands Teemo a fourteen-second window — by far the widest punish window in this lane — and the player had no way to know that from the text.
audit.corrected: A missed Dredge Line is 14s of free poke at rank 1. That is the window to step up in.

audit.whatIsWrong: Teemo's Q was written as "Blinding Shot" in content.mid.
audit.why: Riot's name for Teemo's Q is Blinding Dart.
51.82% over 1868 games — the largest sample in this slice — matches the data already in the file.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 is where I start managing the lane rather than just surviving. My Blinding Shot is fully ranked by now, so any time Nautilus tries to close range I can Q him immediately and his auto-attacks miss through the blind duration — this is my best answer to his trade pattern, because a blinded Nautilus loses the damage he needs to justify hooking in. Stay at E poison range: throw a dart, auto once for the poison stack, then W back out of his hook range before the cooldown refreshes. Never stand still, because standing still hands him a free hook angle. At Level 6 I flip the dynamic: Noxious Trap lets me grid the entire approach lane with mushrooms — place them at the tribush, lane entry, and the two most common hook-throw angles before I show my face. His Dredge Line has to travel through a reveal field that slows him before he can engage, and the shroom slow gives me the W head-start I need to kite back out. This is genuinely my control window and it shows in the lane — he cannot walk up without triggering a shroom, and every hook through shroom-covered ground means I see him coming and W before the anchor hits.

notes: _missing-interactions.json proposes a "knockup-enabler" line for this matchup: "Both sides carry displacement (Noxious Trap (R) vs Dredge Line (Q))". Teemo's mushroom slows, it does not displace — the knockup flag on Noxious Trap in teemo.json is a derivation artifact. I did not write that line. Dredge Line's own displacement is real. Separately, content.win gives Nautilus 6 of 7 stages while Teemo wins 51.82% over 1868 games. The packet did not flag it, and the prose does justify Nautilus owning levels 1-5, so I left the chart alone — but with Teemo owning level 6 outright and this being the biggest sample in the slice, the first-item and 2-item stages are worth a second look by someone with the game data in front of them.
